summary: If guard a1 is nonzero and the byte flag at a2+13 has bit 0x10 set, flush the buffer object a2 via BufferFlushWrite and reset several of its fields: clear the 0x10 bit from the byte at a2+13, and zero the dwords at a2+24, a2+0 and a2+8. Returns the result of BufferFlushWrite on that path.

operations.description: if (a1 != 0) gate the whole flush/reset sequence
test (byte at a2+13) & 0x10; if clear, do nothing
call BufferFlushWrite(a2) to flush the buffer object
clear flag bit 0x10: byte at a2+13 &= 0xEE
return result of BufferFlushWrite on the flush path

unresolved: Return value is uninitialized when either guard fails; the caller-visible contract on those paths is unknown.
Field layout of the a2 object (offset 13 flag byte, offsets 0/8/24 dwords) and what the 0x10 flag means is unproven.
Relationship of the four known callers to the a2 buffer object type is not established.
